I farm only 2 mu, so I count every bag I buy. I do not start from zero. I will follow what I did last year and what the better growers around me do, then make small changes. Here in Quzhou, with well water, wheat and maize can both give a good crop if I do not let fertilizer run short. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. For wheat, I will use improved seed like most people here, keep the land fine with rotary tillage, put more fertilizer on the wheat because it needs a strong stand before winter and good ears in spring, and give about 3 irrigations if the weather is normal. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a bit strong on nitrogen, and use 2 irrigations through the season. On my small area, family labor is enough, so I will manage closely and spray when I see the usual weeds, aphids, armyworm, rust, or leaf disease. I will aim for steady yield, not gamble on saving a small amount of input.
